bare_s1.explanation: The unit mainly responds to road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses), firing on the side body panel near the front door or wheel. It also responds, separately, to dogs.

bare_s2.explanation: The unit responds mainly to road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses), peaking on the body panel near the front wheel or door. It also responds to dogs, a second concept with no meaningful link to vehicles.

Q0_s1.explanation: The unit responds mainly to road vehicles (cars, vans, pickups, buses, emergency vehicles), peaking on the body panel or wheel-arch region. It also responds separately to dogs.

Q0_s2.explanation: The unit responds mainly to road vehicles (cars, trucks, buses, vans), peaking on the side or front body panel near the wheel arch or door. It also responds separately to dogs.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds most strongly to a mid-sized region of smooth, evenly colored, gently curved surface bounded by a crisp contour, with a large dark rounded shape just below and a horizontal edge or seam running across it. It responds more weakly to broad, uniformly toned furry or textured flanks with a similar shape and scale.

F1_s2.explanation: The unit responds to the broad side flank of a large, bulky, side-on body: a fairly uniform surface patch at mid-height, just above and behind a rounded lower contour, often with a crease or seam crossing it. It responds most to smooth, glossy, single-colored versions of this surface and more weakly to soft, textured versions.

wrong.explanation: The unit responds to furry mammal fur/coat texture, most strongly on dogs and dog-like canids (dhole, hyena), especially on the head, ears, and neck/shoulder region. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals such as monkeys, hamsters, squirrels, and minks.
